data.one_liner: Display Apple system-like self-hiding status alerts without interrupting user flow.
data.what_it_does: StatusAlert lets developers display self-hiding system-like status overlays inspired by Apple design guidelines. It supports titles, subtitles, built-in icons, or custom widgets like Rive animations. Only one alert is shown at a time and they automatically dismiss after a configurable duration.
use_when: You want to notify users of non-critical actions (like 'Saved' or 'Subscribed') without blocking interaction.
You need an overlay notification that mimics Apple's system status style.
avoid_when: You need complex notification banners that persist until explicitly dismissed by the user.
You require multiple alerts stacked on top of each other simultaneously.
strengths: Clean, Apple-like system alert presentation with built-in blur support.
Simple imperative API (`StatusAlert.show(...)`) for quick integration.
Supports custom widget configurations such as Rive animations.
weaknesses: Only one alert can be shown at a time; calling `show()` while active does nothing.
`onComplete` is not called when manually dismissed using `StatusAlert.hide()`.

alternatives.name: fluttertoast
alternatives.why_pick_it: If you want simple native-style toast messages across platforms.

alternatives.name: bot_toast
alternatives.why_pick_it: If you need a highly customizable notification and toast system with support for custom overlays.

alternatives.name: another_flushbar
alternatives.why_pick_it: If you prefer top or bottom slide-in flushbars with action buttons and flexible styling.

data.minimal_example:
StatusAlert.show(
  context,
  duration: Duration(seconds: 2),
  title: 'Subscribed',
  subtitle: 'You will be notified of new posts',
  configuration: IconConfiguration(icon: Icons.done),
  maxWidth: 260,
);
